To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HERD's performance is limited by the RDMA network's ability to sustain a high bandwidth; and (2) the performance of RDMA-based key value services depends heavily on the network topology, and the network bandwidth.

HERD is a high-performance key-value service for RDMA networks that uses a combination of RDMA operations and a novel data structure, the RDMA tree, to reduce the latency and improve the throughput of key-value operations.
HERD achieves a throughput of 2.3 million 64-byte requests/sec, which is 2.5 times the throughput of the best RDMA-based system, and 4.5 times the best TCP-based system.
